lesson.grammar_point: verbs followed by gerund or infinitive in recommendations

listenings.text: When I started my career, I wrote legal opinions of twenty pages, and I put the recommendation at the end. My first client refused to read them. He told me, I pay you to decide, not to describe. Since then, I always advise young lawyers to avoid writing ten pages before giving an answer. Put the recommendation in the first paragraph. Then justify it. And never forget two things: the trade-off and an alternative. A client can accept risk. What a client cannot accept is discovering the risk after the decision.

Five years ago, our lawyers recommended waiting six months for the new regulation. We were in a hurry, so we decided to sign immediately. At the time, it seemed like a smart decision. Then the rules changed, and the contract had no safeguard. We had to renegotiate, and in the end we agreed to pay for new equipment that was not in our plan. Now, when a lawyer suggests postponing a decision, I ask one question before deciding: what exactly do we risk losing if we wait, and what do we risk losing if we don't?

The federal government has decided to postpone the tender for the new container port by one year. According to the ministry, the extra time is needed to complete a new feasibility study, after investors refused to accept the traffic numbers in the original documents. Several international groups had planned to bid, and some of them criticized the delay. Others welcomed it. Investors say they expect the new study to include a safeguard against changes in the tariff, and they hope to see the final documents before the end of the year.
